note: THE bare-ok(diagnostic-value) TYPE-AUDIT CLASS CARRIES TWO INCOMPATIBLE MEANINGS, AND THE GUIDANCE FORBIDDING ONE OF THEM IS CONTRADICTED BY SHIPPED CODE. windows/lab/CLAUDE.md documents the class as measurements OF THE IMPLEMENTATION, never of the world, and says in as many words: do not copy that class into anything a world can see. It is describing test-harness durations in timings.rs. But windows/scene/src/lib.rs line 624 tags temperature_grid day parameter and its return bare-ok(diagnostic-value), and a day is a WORLD quantity that a world can very much see. That precedent is committed and drift-checked, so an implementer who greps for how a bare f64 day is tagged finds it, follows it, and lands in the case the lab guide prohibits. Found during The Retelling when a subagent tagged a ladder day the same way and cited scene as precedent. The tag was kept, because following committed precedent is right and rewriting a shared vocabulary was not that campaign scope. WHAT TO DO IF YOU HIT IT: do not silently pick a side. Either the lab sentence is too broad or scene is mistagged, and nothing mechanical can tell you which because type-audit validates that a class is in the closed list, never that it is the RIGHT class. Also worth knowing: reaching for StdDays instead is not a free fix. StdDays is generated by the quantity macro with the positive flag, so a zero day is a constructor error, and a world may legitimately commit an event at day zero.
